questions.q: Which register is the default for news, work email and conversation with strangers?
questions.why: Courant is the middle layer and the one textbooks teach. Soutenu belongs to literature and formal writing, familier to friends and family.

questions.q: You are writing to a client you have never met. Which sentence fits?
choices: J'ai un boulot de dingue en ce moment.
Ça craint, j'ai trop de trucs à faire.
questions.why: Courant with vous is the safe default: never wrong, only slightly formal. The others are familier and would read as over-familiar to a stranger.

questions.q: Order these from soutenu to familier: une bagnole, une automobile, une voiture.
choices: une automobile, une voiture, une bagnole
une voiture, une automobile, une bagnole
une bagnole, une voiture, une automobile
une automobile, une bagnole, une voiture
questions.why: Automobile is soutenu, voiture is the plain courant word, bagnole is familier. Un travail / un boulot and un homme / un mec work the same way.

questions.q: Put « Il n'y a personne. » into familier spoken French, spelled as it sounds.
questions.why: Two things happen at once: ne disappears, and il y a collapses to y'a. The negation still lands, because personne survives.

questions.q: Which is the familier version of « Où allez-vous ? » ?
questions.why: Familier questions lose both inversion and est-ce que, and the question word drifts to the end: tu vas où, tu fais quoi, ça coûte combien.

questions.q: Move it to courant: « J'ai un boulot de dingue. » → J'ai beaucoup de ___ .
questions.why: Boulot is the familier word for travail, and bosser for travailler. Neither belongs in professional writing.

questions.q: Are sympa, télé, resto and prof slang?
choices: Yes, avoid them with anyone you don't know
No — the shortening is completely standard, and the full forms sound stiff
Only télé and resto; the others are slang
questions.why: This clipping is normal French, not argot. It sits apart from genuinely familier vocabulary like bagnole or meuf.

questions.q: « Ce mec est vraiment chelou. » What does chelou mean, and where does it come from?
questions.why: Verlan reverses the syllables: louche gives chelou, lourd gives relou, méchant gives chanmé, fou gives ouf.

questions.q: You are in a work meeting and something goes wrong. Which reaction is a problem?
questions.why: Putain is so frequent in casual French that it can seem harmless. It is vulgar, and in a professional or unfamiliar setting it lands as such.

questions.q: « Ta gueule ! » is aggressive slang. What is the neutral form?
questions.why: La gueule belongs to the vulgar pile. Tais-toi, or taisez-vous with someone you address as vous, is the ordinary way to say it.

questions.q: Which feature marks a text as soutenu?
choices: the passé simple and the imperfect subjunctive
question words at the end of the sentence
questions.why: Soutenu shows up as passé simple, imperfect subjunctive, inversion in questions, the ne explétif, nous rather than on, and veuillez plus infinitive.

questions.q: What is wrong with « Veuillez me filer une clope » ?
choices: It mixes the most formal imperative in French with slang
Clope is not a French word
questions.why: Mixing registers is the giveaway. Pick a level and stay on it: veuillez me donner une cigarette, or file-moi une clope.
Two familier moves in four words: on replaces nous, and cinéma is clipped to ciné. The courant version is nous allons au cinéma.

questions.q: Say the standard closing of a formal French letter.
questions.why: Veuillez plus infinitive is the soutenu imperative, and this formula is fixed. You will write it far less often than you read it.

questions.q: Three phrasings: « Cela ne me convient point », « Ça ne me va pas », « Ça m'va pas ». Say which register each belongs to and name a situation for each.
a: Cela ne me convient point is soutenu: a formal letter, an official complaint, or literature. Ça ne me va pas is courant: the default for work, for a shop, for anyone you address as vous. Ça m'va pas is familier: friends, family, texting. While learning, the safe choice is always the middle one, with vous — French speakers will invite you downwards with on peut se tutoyer.
questions.why: Register is chosen by who you are talking to, not by what you are talking about.
